pharm: A live, attenuated measles virus vaccine that induces protective humoral and cellular immunity against measles (rubeola). It is most often given as part of the combination MMR (measles-mumps-rubella) or MMRV vaccine; a single-antigen measles vaccine is used in some programs.
quick: 0.5 mL subcutaneously; 2 doses >=28 days apart for those without evidence of immunity
CONTRAINDICATED (live virus); avoid pregnancy for 1 month after vaccination
Compatible - breastfeeding is not a contraindication
Observe ~15 minutes for allergic reaction; document dose; ensure 2-dose series
summary: Measles vaccine is a live, attenuated viral vaccine that provides active immunity against measles. In most countries it is given as the combination MMR vaccine (with mumps and rubella) or MMRV (with varicella). The dose is 0.5 mL administered subcutaneously (MMR may also be given IM). The routine schedule is two doses: the first at 12-15 months of age and the second at 4-6 years; older children and adults without evidence of immunity should receive two doses separated by at least 28 days. Two documented doses confer about 97% protection against measles. It is a live vaccine, so it is contraindicated in pregnancy and in significant immunosuppression, and pregnancy should be avoided for one month afterward. This record reflects CDC/ACIP and manufacturer (M-M-R II) guidance.
indications: Active immunization for the prevention of measles (rubeola) in persons 12 months of age and older (and from 6 months in outbreak/travel settings, with later revaccination)
Post-exposure prophylaxis in susceptible immunocompetent individuals when given within 72 hours of measles exposure

dosage.d: 0.5 mL: dose 1 at 12-15 months, dose 2 at 4-6 years
dosage.n: Dose 2 may be given earlier if at least 28 days after dose 1

dosage.c: Older children/adolescents/adults without evidence of immunity
dosage.d: 0.5 mL per dose; two doses at least 28 days apart
dosage.n: Some adults at low risk may need only one dose per local guidance
Does not count toward the routine series; revaccinate with 2 doses on/after the first birthday

dosage.d: 0.5 mL within 72 hours of exposure (susceptible immunocompetent persons)
dosage.n: Immunoglobulin is used instead if vaccine is contraindicated or beyond the window

admin: Reconstitute the lyophilized vaccine only with the supplied diluent; use promptly and protect from light
Administer 0.5 mL subcutaneously (MMR may also be given intramuscularly); the preferred SC site is the upper outer triceps/thigh
May be given simultaneously with other live or inactivated vaccines at separate sites; if not given the same day, separate two live injectable vaccines by at least 28 days
Observe the patient for about 15 minutes after vaccination for immediate allergic reactions; have epinephrine available
moa: The vaccine contains live measles virus that has been attenuated (weakened) so that it replicates to a limited degree without causing disease in immunocompetent hosts. This controlled infection stimulates the immune system to produce measles-specific antibodies and memory B and T cells, conferring durable, often lifelong, protection that mimics natural immunity. Two doses are recommended because a small proportion of recipients do not respond (seroconvert) after a single dose.

absolute: Pregnancy (live virus); avoid becoming pregnant for 1 month after vaccination
Severe immunodeficiency or immunosuppression (e.g., advanced HIV with low CD4, hematologic/solid malignancy under treatment, high-dose corticosteroids, biologics, transplant)
History of anaphylaxis to a previous dose or to a vaccine component (e.g., neomycin, gelatin)
relative: Moderate or severe acute illness with or without fever (defer until recovered)
Recent receipt of antibody-containing blood products/immunoglobulin (defer per recommended intervals)
History of thrombocytopenia or thrombocytopenic purpura
Personal or family history of febrile seizures (small increased febrile seizure risk, especially MMRV)
monitor: Immediate hypersensitivity for ~15 minutes after the dose
Fever and rash 5-12 days after vaccination (expected, transient)
Documentation of doses and evidence of immunity

preg: Live measles vaccine is contraindicated during pregnancy because of a theoretical risk to the fetus from the live attenuated virus. Women should be counseled to avoid becoming pregnant for 1 month (28 days) after vaccination. If a pregnant woman is found to be susceptible, vaccinate after delivery (postpartum). Inadvertent vaccination during pregnancy has not been shown to cause congenital measles syndrome but is still avoided.
lact: Breastfeeding is not a contraindication. Live measles vaccine can be given to nursing mothers; vaccine virus is not transmitted to the infant in a way that causes disease, and breastfeeding does not impair the immune response.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed for renal impairment. Standard caution regarding immunosuppression applies.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed for hepatic impairment. Standard caution regarding immunosuppression applies.

major: Immunosuppressive therapy (high-dose corticosteroids, chemotherapy, biologics, transplant immunosuppression) - contraindicates the live vaccine and blunts the response
Antibody-containing blood products / immunoglobulin - can inhibit the immune response; observe recommended dosing intervals (typically defer the vaccine for several months)
moderate: Other live injectable vaccines - give the same day or separate by at least 28 days
Tuberculin skin test (TST/PPD) and interferon-gamma release assays - may be transiently suppressed; do TST same day as vaccination or defer 4-6 weeks
minor: Salicylate therapy is a concern mainly for varicella-containing vaccines, not measles alone
interactions.diagnostics: May transiently suppress tuberculin reactivity - schedule TB skin testing accordingly.

serious: Febrile seizure (small increased risk, especially with MMRV)
rare: Encephalitis/encephalopathy (very rare, causal relationship not established)
Arthralgia/arthritis (mainly attributable to the rubella component of MMR)
emergency: Anaphylaxis (urticaria, swelling, wheeze, hypotension) shortly after vaccination
Signs of severe bleeding from thrombocytopenia

monitoring: Immediate post-vaccination observation (~15 minutes) for allergic reactions
Expected fever/rash 5-12 days later (reassure, monitor febrile-seizure-prone children)
Documentation of the 2-dose series and immunity status
counsel: This is a live vaccine that protects against measles; two doses give about 97% protection
Mild fever and a faint rash about 1-2 weeks after the shot are common and not contagious
Use acetaminophen for fever/soreness as advised; report a high or prolonged fever or any seizure
Women should avoid getting pregnant for 1 month after this vaccine
Tell your provider if you are pregnant, have a weak immune system, or had a severe allergic reaction to a previous dose, gelatin, or neomycin
Stay about 15 minutes after the shot so staff can watch for any allergic reaction
pk: Protective antibodies develop within about 2-3 weeks of vaccination
Peak antibody response within several weeks
Not applicable - induces durable immune memory
Long-lasting, generally lifelong protection after 2 documented doses
Store the lyophilized vaccine frozen or refrigerated per product label; protect from light; use reconstituted vaccine promptly
pearls: Live attenuated vaccine - usually given as MMR/MMRV; dose is 0.5 mL subcutaneously
Two-dose schedule (12-15 months and 4-6 years) gives ~97% protection; any 2 doses must be >=28 days apart
CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy and significant immunosuppression; avoid pregnancy for 1 month after
Can be used as post-exposure prophylaxis if given within 72 hours to susceptible immunocompetent contacts
Single-antigen measles vaccine and combination MMR are not FDA dietary products - this record reflects CDC/ACIP and M-M-R II labeling
missed: If a scheduled dose is missed, give it as soon as possible - the series does not need to be restarted. Just ensure the two doses are separated by at least 28 days and complete the series.
overdose: Overdose is not a meaningful concern for a single 0.5 mL vaccine dose. Inadvertent administration of an extra dose is not harmful. Manage any local or systemic reactions symptomatically.
